payload_semantics_node.raw: unfiltered driver CSI buffer (wifi_csi_info_t.buf, includes invalid subcarriers); stored verbatim as base64 in frames.csv raw_b64
payload_semantics_node.valid: esp-radar component-filtered payload, layout LLTF | HT-LTF | STBC-HT-LTF; stored verbatim as base64 in frames.csv valid_b64
payload_semantics_node.valid_selection_rule: esp-radar concatenates the enabled LTF sub-ranges of the driver buffer according to csi_config (lltf_en, htltf_en, stbc_htltf2_en); the vendored patch makes that concatenation first_word_invalid-aware, so when the flag is true any range reaching raw bytes 0..3 is clamped to start at byte 4 and the invalid leading pair is not copied. Apart from that clamp no bytes are added, reordered or padded by the recorder
payload_semantics_node.data_type: 0 = int8 (1 byte per component), 1 = int16 little-endian (2 bytes per component)
payload_semantics_node.iq_byte_order: imaginary first, then real (ESP-IDF v5.5.3 api-guides/wifi.rst)
payload_semantics_node.decoding: pairs of (imag, real) components in payload order; slice the LLTF as the leading lltf_len bytes (lltf_len/2 pairs for int8, lltf_len/4 for int16), never a fixed 52 - HT-LTF follows the LLTF segment. No trimming, padding, smoothing or resampling is applied in the browser
payload_semantics_node.first_word_invalid: when true the first four bytes of the driver CSI buffer (raw_b64) are invalid per ESP-IDF v5.5.3 esp_wifi_types_native.h: 2 complex pairs for int8 (data_type 0), 1 pair for int16 (data_type 1). raw_b64 keeps those bytes verbatim; valid_b64 is now produced by a first_word_invalid-aware esp-radar compaction so the invalid leading pair is excluded, which shortens lltf_len/valid_len by 2 bytes (int8) for layouts whose LLTF sub-range reaches raw byte 2 (ESP32 secondary-channel NONE). Consumers reconstruct subcarrier position from lltf_source_ranges + first_word_invalid rather than assuming a fixed 52-pair LLTF
payload_semantics_node.lltf_source_ranges: ESP32 byte offsets into raw_b64 copied into the LLTF segment of valid_b64, before the first_word_invalid clamp: secondary NONE {{76,128},{2,54}} (so recorded LLTF pair 26 was raw pair 1 = bytes 2-3, the invalid word); secondary BELOW/ABOVE {{12,64},{66,118}} (never touch bytes 0-3). int8 pair k occupies raw bytes 2k..2k+1. When first_word_invalid the range start 2 becomes 4, dropping that pair
payload_semantics_node.field_provenance: frames.csv columns seq..rx_gain_compensation, first_word_invalid and rx_seq are native driver/firmware values forwarded verbatim; recording_id, frame_sequence, host_receive_monotonic_ns, payload_ok are host-computed; dropped is the device-side app instrumentation counter value at emission time
payload_semantics_node.clocks: callback_timestamp_us and rx_ctrl_timestamp_us use the device monotonic clock (esp_timer, us); host_receive_monotonic_ns uses the browser performance.now() clock (ms * 1e6); started_at_utc uses the host wall clock. meta.clock_anchor stores a same-instant (performance_now_ms, date_now_ms) pair so host monotonic offsets can be converted to UTC
